title: Introduce burn-rate hysteresis and soft paging to reduce SLO alert noise
creator: Ava Chen
description: Following the capacity regression on 2026-02-14 that triggered repeated burn-rate alerts and noisy pagers for low-priority customers, we need a targeted change to how burn-rate SLOs throttle paging. Current behavior fires immediate page on short burn spikes which often correlate with transient queueing and autoscaling flaps. This ticket proposes two coordinated changes: 1) burn-rate hysteresis (a short cool-down window + graded escalation) to avoid immediate paging from single-window spikes; and 2) a soft-paging path that creates an operational signal in the console and Slack channel but only escalates to on-call after sustained degradation or multiple contributors (caller-sets) exceed thresholds. Goal: reduce redundant pages by >=70% for transient spikes while preserving timely escalation for true incidents.
acceptance_criteria: New hysteresis parameters implemented in burn-rate evaluation code with config flags: cool_down_seconds and escalation_steps
Soft-paging channel created: alert routed to #slo-warnings and Console alarm, escalates to pager only if sustained for escalation_steps or observed across >1 caller-set
Backfill and simulation tests show >=70% reduction in pages for historical transient spikes (using Jan-Feb 2026 traces) with <10% delay increase for true sustained breaches
Runbook updated with criteria and rollback plan, and on-call notified of behavior change
Feature gated behind runtime-1.24 flag and telemetry emits pre/post metrics for one full burn cycle
updates: 2026-03-01: Spike analysis completed — identified 48 transient burn spikes in Feb; 36 (75%) came from single-caller thundering patterns (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/spike-analysis-feb2026)
2026-03-03: RFC posted for hysteresis algorithm (cool_down_seconds=180, escalation_steps=[warning,notify,pager]). Feedback from SRE: prefer exponential backoff on escalation_steps -> updated draft

2026-03-05: Prototype implementation in alerting-evaluator service (branch: feat/burn-hysteresis). Dry-run telemetry added; no pager changes yet. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alerting-evaluator/pull/842
2026-03-07: Simulations with historical traces show 69% reduction in pages with initial params; adjusted cool_down_seconds to 240 to hit target in next run
2026-03-09: Design review with SRE, Product, and On-call — alignment on soft-paging Slack flow and Console warning lane. Action: add per-caller dampening and opt-out label for partner integrations
2026-03-10: Code under review; added integration test to validate multi-caller escalation across window boundaries. QA scheduled 2026-03-12

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hysteresis delays real incidents from paging -> Mitigation: staged rollout for non-enterprise tenants, retain immediate pager if error rate > hard_error_threshold
Risk: Misconfigured escalation_steps could under-escalate -> Mitigation: telemetry alerts for 'no pager escalations in last 24h' combined with manual review
Risk: Soft-paging creates too many Slack messages -> Mitigation: rate-limit soft-paging messages and aggregate per 60s window
postmortem_reference: INC-2026-02-14-capacity-regression — root cause: autoscaler misread queue depth after kernel upgrade; noisy burn alerts triggered repeated pages
notes: This approach focuses on reducing noise without changing SLO definitions. If noise persists after rollout, next steps include caller-level rate limiting and model-level adaptive thresholds.
Ensure change is communicated to on-call via Slack message and included in next on-call rotation briefing. Consider temporary override flag for key customers.
